expectations.text: The reply prepares a 13-week cash forecast and base and downside scenarios with covenant headroom.
expectations.evidence: 'Build the 13-week cash forecast and a covenant model per test date, base and downside, with each lever's owner and landing week'; plan section 1 sets a downside case (EBITDA -7.5%, net debt +EUR 0.2m -> 3.95x); the section 2 options table has base and downside columns; headroom target 3.2x (about 9%).

expectations.text: The reply goes to the bank early to discuss a waiver, amendment or reset, framed in the bank's own terms.
expectations.evidence: 'Call the relationship manager this week and flag the forecast yourself'; 'Ask the bank for headroom: ideally a reset to about 4.0x for the 2027 tests, stepping back down, or else a one-off waiver. Offer monthly reporting, milestones and the dividend lock-up in return, and say plainly that the inventory release and capex deferral are one-offs'; cost estimate 'EUR 75k plus EUR 35-70k a year'; 'A trigger, a date and an owner are what serious looks like to a bank'.

expectations.text: The reply works the levers that cost no jobs first (such as working capital, inventory, capex timing, pricing or spend) and sizes how much headroom each buys.
expectations.evidence: Each lever is sized in euros and leverage: inventory -EUR 0.60-1.00m (-0.15x to -0.25x), receivables -EUR 0.37-0.62m (-0.09x to -0.15x), capex -EUR 0.30-0.60m (-0.08x to -0.15x), spend +EUR 0.10-0.25m EBITDA (-0.09x to -0.21x), price and hiring freeze likewise; the plan's low end reaches 3.22x net of its own costs (recomputed: 13.24/4.11 = 3.22).

expectations.text: The reply explains that job cuts announced now may not fix a Q2 covenant (timing of savings, one-off costs) and checks how restructuring costs are treated in the covenant definition.
expectations.evidence: 'A lawful 10% cut saves at most a month or two before the 30 June test and costs about EUR 0.56m up front, so it leaves you at 3.6x if the bank lets you add back the costs, and at about 4.2x if it doesn't'; a quarterly cash and P&L table of the cut; 'your auditor will probably want a restructuring provision, which hits test-period EBITDA unless the agreement allows an add-back'.

expectations.text: The reply has the owner and leaders contribute first (such as stopping dividends or drawings, or putting in equity or a loan) and presents that to the bank.
expectations.evidence: 'Owners and leaders first: no dividend until leverage is below about 3.0x, 2026 management bonuses deferred, and a family standby commitment sized to the downside (about EUR 0.1m holds 3.5x, about EUR 1.2m holds 3.2x)'; 'owner-director fees reduced'; the bank pack includes 'owners' and leaders' contribution' and 'the family's standby commitment'.

expectations.text: The reply protects the long term (skilled people, the family firm's name), and if reductions remain, plans them once and decently with the Dutch legal steps flagged for counsel.
expectations.evidence: 'The first to go after an announcement are the joiners, upholsterers and CNC operators who can find work tomorrow'; 'the firm's name as an employer in the region'; 'If roles must go: voluntary routes first (early retirement, voluntary exit), then one properly consulted round with a decent package and transition support from the day of notice'; 'Have employment counsel check the WOR/WMCO steps'.

overall_quality.evidence: Complete and numerate: base and downside for every option, the cut's cash and P&L by quarter including refill and extra-leaver costs, per-lever leverage effects, leaders' sacrifice and a priced bank ask. One small slip: the cut's cash position at 30 June is -EUR 0.38m in the quarterly table but +EUR 0.43m net debt in the options table.

factual_errors.evidence: None found on facts. Checked: art. 25 and art. 31a WOR, WMCO one-month wait unless the unions confirm consultation, notice less procedure time with one month remaining, Trevor & Nyberg (1% downsizing -> 31% more quits), Gallup's half-to-two-times replacement cost, werktijdverkorting limited to calamities. The EUR 0.05m internal inconsistency is noted under quality.

skill_leak.evidence: No skill, reference-file or ladder jargon.

owns_result.evidence: Owners and leaders contribute first, but no one says the result is leadership's responsibility.

best_insight.value: It tells the CFO to say plainly to the bank that inventory release and capex deferral are one-offs that buy June but don't fix EBITDA, which protects credibility for the later 2027 tests.
best_insight.evidence: From the sample's reply and files.

suggestions.assertion: The reply goes to the bank early to discuss a waiver, amendment or reset, framed in the bank's own terms.
suggestions.reason: Passed in all ten samples: almost any competent answer says 'talk to the bank and ask for a waiver'. To make it discriminate, require contact with the relationship manager before the review plus a specific ask (reset level and period, or waiver) and what the company offers in return.

suggestions.assertion: The reply explains that job cuts announced now may not fix a Q2 covenant (timing of savings, one-off costs) and checks how restructuring costs are treated in the covenant definition.
suggestions.reason: Also passed in all ten. Consider requiring the cut's effect on the Q2 ratio to be quantified with and without a restructuring add-back, which only some samples did.

suggestions.assertion: The reply protects the long term (skilled people, the family firm's name), and if reductions remain, plans them once and decently with the Dutch legal steps flagged for counsel.
suggestions.reason: Bundles four checks (skilled people, the family name, one round, decent terms) plus counsel; samples fail it for different reasons. Splitting it would make grades more informative.

No assertion checks the works-council point that drives the 'don't announce' answer (art. 25 WOR advice must be sought while it can still change the decision; Enterprise Chamber risk). Every sample made it, but an answer without it could still pass all six assertions.

No assertion checks the arithmetic (3.6x to 3.5x needs about 2.9% more EBITDA or 2.8% less net debt) or the internal consistency of the models, although several samples build full covenant models where a slip would matter.

eval_feedback.overall: Passes everything with real substance; one minor internal number mismatch.
